texts: "The authorities could try to bypass the veto from the French & Georgian citoyenne who leads the country."
"The authorities might try to bypass the veto from the géorgienne who leads the nation." (Note: I maintained "géorgienne" in French as it was part of the person's identity in the original sentence.)
"The authorities might try to bypass the opposition of the citoyenne who leads Georgia from France." (Note: 'citoyenne' is kept in French as the 10th word)
The authorities might attempt to bypass the veto of citoyenne Georgia's and France's citizen who leads the country.
